title: an external project's macOS round can read its own worktree's git directory again: the pinned-folder deny that hides the project home no longer hides the managed clone's .git, so git works in the round exactly as in a self round
acceptance: Why. The T-055 pilot's first external rounds (project the pilot external project, task T-001, rounds worker-pilar-t001-r1b at 21:18 and worker-pilar-t001-r1c at 21:42 on 2026-10-05, codex on macOS) both stopped at their first command: `git status` in the worktree <external project path> failed with `fatal: not a git repository: <external project path>`. The worktree's `.git` file and the admin directory were correct, and `git status` worked outside the sandbox. Cause, reproduced with the round's own code snapshot (state/snapshots/code-3z8afgqf/bin/fm-sandbox.sh run, the round's policy.json, --vendor=codex, `zsh -lc 'git status'`, no model) on a fixture external home: with FM_PINNED_DIR set and FM_EXTERNAL=0 git works (rc 0); with FM_EXTERNAL=1 it fails with exactly that message (rc 128). `pinned_state()` (bin/lib/fm_sandbox_policy.py:188-191) returns the project home `<home>` (the parent of `<home>/state`) for an external round, and `darwin()` writes `(deny file-read* file-write* (subpath <home>))` (:236-237) after the reads allow (:228). The round's own roots and the pinned folder are allowed again afterwards (:246-250), but the git directories `gitdirs()` adds to the reads (:88-104, used at :787 in main(): the worktree's admin dir `<home>/repo/.git/worktrees/<task>` and the common dir `<home>/repo/.git`) are not, so SBPL's last-rule-wins leaves them unreadable and git's is_git_directory check fails. A self round is unaffected: its gitdirs are under the engine's `.git`, not under `pinned_state` (`<engine>/state`). Linux is unaffected: `linux()` hides the pinned state with a tmpfs only when that state lies under a read root (:290-293), and `<home>` lies under none (the gitdirs are below it, not above it), so the gitdirs' `--ro-bind-try` binds stand.

The fix, in bin/lib/fm_sandbox_policy.py `darwin()` only. Immediately after the line that denies `pinned_state(pinned)` (and before the roots allow), when a pinned folder is granted, write one rule `(allow file-read* (subpath <g>) ...)` for exactly those git directories g returned by `gitdirs(roots[0])` that lie at or below `pinned_state(pinned)` and at or below no `never_read` entry (prefix test with a trailing '/', the same comparison `linux()` uses). Directly after that allow, write `(deny file-read* file-write* (subpath <n>) ...)` for every `never_read` entry n that lies at or below one of the allowed git directories (same prefix test), so a never-readable path inside the clone's .git stays denied on macOS as it already is on Linux (where `linux()` hides never_read entries under any read root, :303-311); skip that deny line when no such entry exists. When the git directory list is empty - every self round, every round without a pinned folder, every external round whose clone is outside the home - write nothing, so those profiles stay byte-identical to today's. The rule grants read only: no write to the clone's .git, the same as a self round today (rounds never commit; the launcher commits outside the round). It grants nothing else under the home: CONVENTIONS.md, design.md, tasks/, state/ (signing key, other runs) and the managed clone's working tree stay denied by the existing pinned_state deny; the pinned folder and the round's own roots keep their existing allows. Compute the list from the same real root `main()` passes to `gitdirs()` at :787 (`real(root)`); `roots[0]` equals it for every current policy because `{root}` is the first write entry (bin/lib/fm_registry.py:469), but pass the root explicitly into `darwin()` rather than relying on that order. No change to `linux()`, `pinned_state()`, `gitdirs()`, policy generation (bin/fm-config.sh fm_policy), the adapters or fm-sandbox.sh.

The T-177 frozen baseline stays frozen. tests/lib/t177_sandbox_base.py says 'Reference only: do not update to match the implementation' and its body is pinned by `test_reference_is_frozen` (tests/lib/launcher_python.py:168-170, sha256 179015cc…a31a6); neither the file nor that hash changes. `test_every_adapter_profile_is_byte_identical` (:172-228) will now differ in exactly one kind of case: its fixture's tree has a `.git` file naming `<home>/git/worktrees/fixture` with commondir `../..`, and the pinned folder is `<home>/state/runs/fixture/pinned`, so with FM_EXTERNAL=1 (listeners 'unknown', :213-214) `pinned_state` is `<home>` and both git directories lie under it. Change that test in launcher_python.py so that, for role worker, platform darwin, listeners 'unknown', the expected stdout is the base module's stdout with exactly one line inserted immediately after the line `(deny file-read* file-write* (subpath "<home>"))`: `(allow file-read* (subpath "<home>/git/worktrees/fixture") (subpath "<home>/git"))` (path quoting as the module's `sub()` writes it; no never_read entry lies inside those directories, so no re-deny line follows). Every other case (all of linux, darwin with listeners '' or '4317,5511', and the reviewer role, whose `.git` is a directory so `gitdirs()` returns []) still compares byte for byte, return codes and stderr included. Assert the inserted-line case per vendor so a wrong order or an extra line fails.

Tests (in tests/lib/pinned_context.py, next to `test_real_sandbox_reads_pinned_but_denies_writes_key_and_other_run`, :273 onward, using its skip rules: skip when the OS sandbox tool is missing or FM_IN_ROUND=1):
(a) real sandbox, darwin and linux: build an external home fixture `<root>/private` with `git init` of `repo`, one commit, `git -C repo worktree add <root>/private/worktrees/T-218 -b t218`, a pinned folder `<root>/private/state/runs/worker-x/pinned` (made the way the existing fixture makes it, so pinned_of() accepts it), CONVENTIONS.md, design.md and tasks/T-218.json under `private`, and a key file under `private/state`. Policy as the existing test's, with never_read=[str(private/state)] and read covering the toolchain only (not `<root>`). Generate the profile with FM_EXTERNAL=1 and FM_PINNED_DIR set, `--root=<worktree>`, and run inside it: `git -C <worktree> rev-parse --git-dir` prints the admin dir and exits 0; `git -C <worktree> status --porcelain` exits 0; reading `private/CONVENTIONS.md`, `private/design.md`, `private/tasks/T-218.json`, the key and another run's file each fails; writing a file under `private/repo/.git` fails; the pinned design.md is still readable and not writable. Fail-first: on base the git commands fail on darwin (exit 128, `not a git repository`); the linux variant is a regression guard (green on base).
(b) profile text, no sandbox needed (FM_SANDBOX_OS=darwin): with the same fixture and FM_EXTERNAL=1, the profile contains `(allow file-read* (subpath "<private>/repo/.git/worktrees/T-218")` and `(subpath "<private>/repo/.git")` on one allow line placed after the `(deny file-read* file-write* (subpath "<private>"))` line and before the roots allow; with FM_EXTERNAL=0 (the pinned folder under an engine-style `<root>/engine/state/runs/...` and the worktree's git outside it) the profile has no such line and equals tests/lib/t177_sandbox_base.py's output for the same arguments. Fail-first: the line is absent on base.
(c) never_read guards (profile text, FM_SANDBOX_OS=darwin, FM_EXTERNAL=1): (c1) when a never_read entry covers the clone (never_read includes `<private>/repo`), no git-directory allow line is written; (c2) when a never_read entry lies inside the clone's .git (never_read includes `<private>/repo/.git/hooks`), the allow line is written and is followed by `(deny file-read* file-write* (subpath "<private>/repo/.git/hooks"))`, and in the real-sandbox case (a) on darwin, when that entry is added to the policy, reading a file in `<private>/repo/.git/hooks` fails while `git rev-parse --git-dir` still succeeds. (c1) is a regression guard (green on base); (c2)'s ordering check is fail-first with (b).
Use only assertions tests/lib.sh or unittest provide (no unittest.mock assert_* names in tests/*.sh); new temp directories via the existing helpers, never bare `mktemp -d`.

Callers and fixtures, checked by grep: `pinned_state` is used only in bin/lib/fm_sandbox_policy.py (:188 definition, :237 darwin, :291 linux) and mirrored in tests/lib/t177_sandbox_base.py (:177, :226, :280). `gitdirs` is defined at :88 and used at :787. FM_PINNED_DIR is exported by bin/lib/fm-pinned.sh:5 (sourced by bin/fm-worker.sh:1265 and bin/fm-review.sh:825) and by bin/lib/fm-spec-preflight.sh:57, read by bin/adapters/_lib.sh and bin/lib/fm_prompt_context.py:176, and by tests/lib/pinned_context.py, role_prompts.py, launcher_python.py, spec-pin-worker.test.sh, spec-pin-review.test.sh, review-diff.test.sh; none of these asserts the absence of a gitdir allow, and none changes. The real-sandbox suites tests/sandbox-os.test.sh and tests/sandbox-policy.test.sh do not set FM_EXTERNAL with a pinned folder (grep); they stay unchanged. Other FM_EXTERNAL=1 tests (tests/external-*.test.sh, stacking_cases.py, evidence_binding.py) do not generate sandbox profiles and stay unchanged.

Docs, edited in place: design/design.md §13.2 (the paragraph '**The tree's link to git cannot be destroyed from inside - a worker's worktree only.**', about :4291) gains two sentences: an external round's pinned-folder deny covers the whole project home, so the profile re-allows read (only read) of the round's own git directories under it after that deny, on macOS; Linux needs no rule because it never hides the home. And §15.7 where T-173's sandbox-protected `pinned/` folder is described (about :5357): one sentence that the external home stays hidden except the pinned folder, the round's roots and the round's own git directories (read-only, with any never_read entry inside them still denied).

In flight and migration. No stored record or policy format changes. Rounds run on frozen code snapshots, so a round already running keeps its old profile; the next external round after the merge (the T-055 pilot's T-001, redispatched by firstmate) gets the fix. Self rounds and Linux rounds produce byte-identical profiles. The autopilot reloads by itself after the merge (T-203). No other open PR touches bin/lib/fm_sandbox_policy.py.

Evidence is this PR's required GitHub check and the six gates 1, 2, 4, 5, 6, 7. Workers do not run the suites. The CI runner is Linux, so the darwin real-sandbox case (a) is exercised on macOS by firstmate's gates and by the profile-text case (b) on every platform; fail-first is expected from (b) and from (a) on macOS.
